# Bludle

> Bludle is an independent collection of free browser puzzle games created by Stuart Pecksen. Games cover words, colour perception, logic, visual and musical memory, and reaction speed. No download is required.

- Canonical site: https://bludle.com/
- Creator and contact: https://bludle.com/about/
- Editorial policy: https://bludle.com/editorial-policy/
- Journal: https://bludle.com/blogs/
- Sitemap: https://bludle.com/sitemap.xml
- Last updated: 2026-08-19

## Games

### Word games

- [Werdle](https://bludle.com/werdle/): Play Werdle free: solve a five-letter daily word in five tries, reveal its origin, or switch to unlimited practice with no sign-up. Format: Daily puzzle and unlimited practice. Typical round: About 3–5 minutes.
- [Bludle](https://bludle.com/bludle/): Play Bludle free and decode a five-letter word from shades of blue, with A at the light end and Z at the darkest end of the alphabet spectrum. Format: Daily visual word puzzle. Typical round: About 2–4 minutes.
- [Codle](https://bludle.com/codle/): Play Codle free and decode five-letter word ciphers built from shifting, mirroring, reversing and alternating alphabet rules. Format: Progressive code-breaking rounds. Typical round: About 3–6 minutes.
- [Connex](https://bludle.com/connex/): Sort sixteen words into four hidden groups by finding the connection shared by each set. Format: Browser word-association puzzle. Typical round: About 5–10 minutes.
- [Word Mash](https://bludle.com/wordmash/): Build a chain of overlapping words by finding the shared letters that join one answer to the next. Format: Daily overlap puzzle. Typical round: About 3–5 minutes.
- [Glyph](https://bludle.com/glyph/): Identify daily words from their typographic silhouettes before the individual letters are revealed. Format: Five daily silhouette puzzles. Typical round: About 3–6 minutes.
- [Borrowed Letters](https://bludle.com/borrowedletters/): Repair five clue answers whose misplaced letters have been passed around a circular chain. Format: Daily circular word puzzle. Typical round: About 5–8 minutes.

### Colour games

- [Shifty Fades](https://bludle.com/shiftyfades/): Find the exact target colour among near matches across fifty increasingly subtle levels. Format: Fifty progressive levels. Typical round: About 2–8 minutes.
- [Colour Match](https://bludle.com/colormatch/): Recreate the daily target colour by adjusting its red, green and blue channels, then compare both RGB values. Format: One daily target and one submission. Typical round: About 2–4 minutes.
- [Afterimage](https://bludle.com/afterimage/): Memorise a colour, wait for it to disappear, and rebuild it from RGB controls across five daily rounds. Format: Five daily memory rounds. Typical round: About 4–7 minutes.
- [Chroma Lock](https://bludle.com/chromalock/): Stop a cycling colour at the instant it matches the target in a compact visual timing puzzle. Format: Progressive timing challenge. Typical round: About 2–5 minutes.
- [Guess Hue](https://bludle.com/guesshue/): Play Guess Hue free: spot the one different colour in four seconds as each successful round makes the hue difference more subtle. Format: Endless four-second rounds. Typical round: Usually 1–5 minutes.
- [Tintuition](https://bludle.com/tintuition/): Match colours by eye using HSL controls, build combos and climb through increasingly exact ranks. Format: Ranked colour-matching run. Typical round: About 3–8 minutes.

### Logic games

- [XY Marks the Spot](https://bludle.com/hunt/): Use coordinate, direction and distance clues to locate hidden treasure before your limited scans run out. Format: Guided demo then puzzle rounds. Typical round: About 3–6 minutes.
- [Seequence](https://bludle.com/seequence/): Memorise a colour sequence, then reproduce the exact pattern after it disappears. Format: Progressive memory streak. Typical round: About 2–6 minutes.
- [Dead Centre](https://bludle.com/deadcentre/): Memorise a target, wait for it to vanish, and click its exact centre across eight daily spatial-memory rounds. Format: Eight daily spatial rounds. Typical round: About 3–5 minutes.

### Speed games

- [Reaction](https://bludle.com/reaction/): Measure how quickly you respond to a visual change through short, repeatable browser reaction tests. Format: Repeatable reaction trials. Typical round: Under 2 minutes.
- [Alternate](https://bludle.com/alternate/): React to each colour switch and stretch a five-second time budget through a fast sequence of accurate responses. Format: Five-second reaction run. Typical round: Under 1 minute.
- [Trak](https://bludle.com/trak/): Follow a moving signal after it disappears and stop it inside changing targets on lines, curves, circles and shaped tracks. Format: Progressive visual tracking levels. Typical round: About 2–6 minutes.

### Audio games

- [Heardle](https://bludle.com/heardle/): Listen to a sequence of musical notes, then recreate the melody from memory before your lives run out. Format: Melody memory game. Typical round: About 2–5 minutes.

## Access

Pages are public and may be crawled when permitted by robots.txt. Individual game pages are the authoritative source for current rules and formats.


## Detailed game notes

### Werdle

- URL: https://bludle.com/werdle/
- Category: Word
- How to play: Enter any five letters; guesses do not need to be valid words. Green letters are correct, amber letters belong elsewhere, and grey letters are not in the answer. Find the word within five tries.
- Distinguishing mechanic: Werdle keeps the familiar deduction loop but adds a word-origin reveal, so every solved puzzle ends with something worth learning.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Bludle

- URL: https://bludle.com/bludle/
- Category: Word
- How to play: Read each blue tile as a letter value: A is the lightest end of the scale and Z is the darkest. Translate the five shades, submit a word, and use the new colour evidence to refine it.
- Distinguishing mechanic: Bludle turns spelling into visual decoding. The alphabet-to-colour mapping never changes, so pattern recognition improves naturally with repeated play.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Codle

- URL: https://bludle.com/codle/
- Category: Word
- How to play: Study the encoded word and the active rule, then reverse that transformation to recover the answer. Later rounds combine less familiar rules and require closer comparison.
- Distinguishing mechanic: Each puzzle asks you to understand a transformation rather than memorise a single offset, making Codle a compact test of language and logical flexibility.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Connex

- URL: https://bludle.com/connex/
- Category: Word
- How to play: Select four words that share a precise connection and submit the group. Correct groups lock into place; incorrect attempts encourage you to reconsider overlaps and red herrings.
- Distinguishing mechanic: Connex rewards lateral thinking because plausible relationships often cross the intended groups. The challenge is finding the most exact explanation.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Word Mash

- URL: https://bludle.com/wordmash/
- Category: Word
- How to play: Use the clues to solve neighbouring words, then inspect where the end of one answer can become the beginning of another. Every overlap must make the whole chain work.
- Distinguishing mechanic: Word Mash combines clue solving with structural reasoning: a likely answer is only useful when it also supports its neighbours.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Glyph

- URL: https://bludle.com/glyph/
- Category: Word
- How to play: Inspect the outline made by ascenders, descenders and letter widths. Enter a word that fits the silhouette, or reveal an optional clue when shape alone is not enough.
- Distinguishing mechanic: Glyph makes the normally invisible shape of written language into the clue, producing a word game that feels distinct from letter-colour deduction.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Borrowed Letters

- URL: https://bludle.com/borrowedletters/
- Category: Word
- How to play: Solve each clue, spot the letter that does not belong, and move the borrowed letters between neighbouring answers until every word is repaired.
- Distinguishing mechanic: Every answer affects two others, so progress comes from combining vocabulary with whole-system reasoning rather than solving clues in isolation.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Shifty Fades

- URL: https://bludle.com/shiftyfades/
- Category: Colour
- How to play: Compare the target with the candidate swatches and select the exact match. Differences become smaller as the level rises, so early instinct gives way to careful comparison.
- Distinguishing mechanic: The difficulty curve is visible and immediate: the task never changes, but your eye must become more precise.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Colour Match

- URL: https://bludle.com/colormatch/
- Category: Colour
- How to play: Study the target, adjust the red, green and blue controls, and submit your closest mix. The result reveals the target RGB beside your values and scores the total channel difference.
- Distinguishing mechanic: Colour Match turns an intuitive visual judgement into understandable numeric feedback without revealing the answer before commitment.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Afterimage

- URL: https://bludle.com/afterimage/
- Category: Colour
- How to play: Study each colour during the viewing phase. Once it vanishes, reconstruct it with the RGB controls and submit to see the target and your remembered mix together.
- Distinguishing mechanic: Removing the reference separates colour memory from ordinary matching and shows how quickly a precise visual impression drifts.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Chroma Lock

- URL: https://bludle.com/chromalock/
- Category: Colour
- How to play: Memorise the target colour, watch the active colour cycle, and lock it when the two match. Accurate stops advance the run while misses expose the difference.
- Distinguishing mechanic: Chroma Lock mixes perception with timing: recognising the correct colour is only half the problem; you must act at the right instant.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Guess Hue

- URL: https://bludle.com/guesshue/
- Category: Colour
- How to play: Scan the colour grid and select the tile whose hue differs from the rest. A correct choice extends the streak and reduces the colour gap; a miss ends the run.
- Distinguishing mechanic: The four-second limit keeps perception instinctive, while the adaptive hue gap gives every streak a natural difficulty curve.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Tintuition

- URL: https://bludle.com/tintuition/
- Category: Colour
- How to play: Adjust hue, saturation and lightness until your colour looks like the target, then lock the answer. Accuracy and remaining time combine into points and combo progress.
- Distinguishing mechanic: HSL mirrors the way people describe colour—tone, intensity and lightness—making the feedback easier to learn from than raw guessing.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### XY Marks the Spot

- URL: https://bludle.com/hunt/
- Category: Logic
- How to play: Choose a coordinate to scan. The game reports the direction and distance to the hidden point; combine successive clues to eliminate locations and make the final find.
- Distinguishing mechanic: The required demonstration teaches the coordinate idea with visible possibilities, while real rounds remove those highlights and leave the deduction to you.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Seequence

- URL: https://bludle.com/seequence/
- Category: Logic
- How to play: Watch the sequence without making choices, hold the order in memory, and reproduce it only when playback ends. Longer patterns follow successful answers.
- Distinguishing mechanic: The interface separates watching from answering, so the challenge measures the sequence you retained rather than your ability to copy it live.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Dead Centre

- URL: https://bludle.com/deadcentre/
- Category: Logic
- How to play: Study the target while the canvas is passive. When it disappears and the guessing phase begins, place one marker where you remember its centre and receive a distance score.
- Distinguishing mechanic: Changing target sizes and positions make each round a clean test of spatial memory rather than cursor tracking.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Heardle

- URL: https://bludle.com/heardle/
- Category: Audio
- How to play: Play the target melody, remember the order of its notes, then select C, D, E, F and G to rebuild the sequence. Submit the composition to score it; successful rounds become longer and introduce more notes.
- Distinguishing mechanic: Heardle combines musical listening with sequence memory: it asks you to reproduce an original note pattern, not identify a commercial song or artist.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Reaction

- URL: https://bludle.com/reaction/
- Category: Speed
- How to play: Start a trial, wait without anticipating, and respond the moment the visual signal changes. Repeated attempts produce a more useful picture than a single lucky click.
- Distinguishing mechanic: The restrained presentation keeps attention on the signal and makes it easy to compare attempts without downloads or setup.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Alternate

- URL: https://bludle.com/alternate/
- Category: Speed
- How to play: Wait for the state to switch, respond immediately, and repeat. Correct reactions preserve the run; hesitation consumes the shared clock.
- Distinguishing mechanic: Alternate replaces a conventional submitted score with an immediate personal run, keeping the ending quick and replayable.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.

### Trak

- URL: https://bludle.com/trak/
- Category: Speed
- How to play: Watch the signal establish its speed and path. Continue tracking it mentally after it vanishes, then stop it when you believe it has entered the target zone.
- Distinguishing mechanic: Later tracks add curves, loops, letter-like paths and smaller stopping zones, expanding one simple timing action into a varied focus challenge.
- Access: Free browser game; no download required.
